title: headcount-debrief-action-items
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal prep + action item tracker for Monday headcount sync and interview loop debriefs. Meant to be a lightweight scratchpad — will transfer final asks to Confluence and create JIRA tickets after sync.

Agenda for 1:1 / headcount sync (30m)
- 5m: Quick state (open reqs, pipeline counts)
- 10m: Interview loop debriefs + calibration (who to move forward, feedback alignment)
- 10m: Prioritization + budget alignment (which reqs to accelerate / pause)
- 5m: Actions & owners

Current pipeline summary (subjective counts)
- SWE backend: 6 active candidates (2 onsite scheduled), 1 strong offer-ready (SWE-B-101).
- Infra SRE: 4 active, pipeline thin for linux/TF skillset.
- Research infra: 3 screened (need better LLM infra candidates).
- PM: 2 strong, 1 neutral.

Open reqs and ask this cycle
- SWE-B (backend infra) — priority: high (Q2 production rollout). Headcount ask: 2 FTEs.
- SRE (platform) — priority: medium-high. Ask: 1 FTE + contractor.
- Research infra (applied-ml infra) — priority: medium. Ask: 1 FTE.
- Console PM — priority: low. Hold until Q3.

Interview loop debrief notes (roundup)
- Candidate A (SWE-B): strong system design, clear latency/cost tradeoffs, flagged on a couple of small API design mismatches. Recommend move to onsite + exec lunch.
- Candidate B (SRE): good troubleshooting + k8s ops. Interviewers noted limited depth on profiling/AT-scale debugging. Suggest take-home assignment?
- Candidate C (Research infra): excellent on quantization + runtimes. Compensation ask high; check budget/benchmarks.

Calibration / unresolved questions
- Consistency on rubric: some interviewers used 5-point scale, others used pass/fail. Need short alignment doc for loop scoring (quick 3-pt rubric: skills, ownership, fit).
- Compensation guardrails: do we have flexibility to go above band for Research infra roles? (Talk to finance before offer).
- Should we convert contractor for SRE into headcount if we can't find right fit? Cost/coverage analysis needed.

Action items (owner -> due)
- Create quick scoring rubric for interview loops and share with interviewers (owner: Nora) -> due 2026-03-03.
- Sync with Finance re: compensation flexibility for Research infra role (owner: Priya) -> due 2026-02-28.
- Draft candidate A offer template + target salary range (owner: Liam) -> due 2026-03-01.
- Open JIRA ticket to spin up contractor for SRE (owner: Marcus) -> due 2026-03-02.
- Move accepted candidates to Confluence offer tracker and notify TA (owner: Liam) -> due 2026-03-04.

Notes / talking points for headcount sync
- Emphasize SLO-driven hiring: SWE-B hires are critical for Q2 latency/cost work; argue for 2 headcount.
- Tradeoffs: delay Console PM to Q3 to reallocate budget to Research infra if necessary.
- Backup plan: if Research infra comp cannot be met, prioritize internal upskill + contractor for short term.

Quick TODO list (personal)
- [ ] Finalize offer numbers for Candidate A
- [ ] Send calendar invite for calibration session with interviewers (30m)
- [ ] Update Confluence headcount table after sync

Links/references (to paste into Confluence later)
- Recruiting pipeline spreadsheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/recruiting-pipeline-2026
- Headcount plan (Confluence): CONFLUENCE-ORG/headcount-plan-2026
- Related JIRA tickets: JIRA-RECRUIT-178, JIRA-ENG-402

Freeform notes / thoughts
- Might be useful to run a 1-hour calibration workshop next month to tighten rubrics; could reduce false negatives.
- Consider a short one-pager for hiring managers summarizing compensation bands and approval steps (helps speed offers).
- Keep an eye on Dedicated product hiring velocity — if we miss 2 hires this quarter, may need to reprioritize rollout features.

End of notes. Will refine after sync and create final artifacts in shared_drives/product/people-ops.)
